name: zokio
workload: Microbenchmarks of async_fn creation, await execution, task scheduling, memory allocation and I/O ops/sec, compared against stated approximate Tokio baseline figures
claimed_speedup: Claims 32x-96x faster than Tokio across microbenchmarks (e.g. task scheduling 145M ops/s vs ~1.5M ops/s; async_fn creation 3.2B ops/s vs ~100M ops/s)
tradeoffs: Compile-time-heavy Zig async design; extremely low adoption (5 stars) for the scale of claims made.
caveats: Tokio baseline numbers are given as approximate ("~100M ops/sec", "~50M ops/sec") rather than measured on the same hardware/run as the Zokio numbers; ratios of 32x-96x for what should be comparable primitive operations are implausible and likely compare non-equivalent workloads. Capped at tier C per the >50x implausibility rule; treat with strong skepticism.
found_via: GitHub: gh search code "faster than tokio" -> louloulin/zokio docs/en/performance.md

verification.tier_reason: The performance guide states Zig 0.14.0 -O ReleaseFast on an Apple M1 Pro, and comparison code exists (benchmarks/tokio_vs_zokio_direct_comparison.zig, src/bench/tokio_runner.zig). But the Tokio column is approximate ('~100M ops/sec') and not shown to come from a same-machine run, and the >50x ratios on microbenchmarks are implausible, so this is first-party and falls short of a reproducible A: tier C.
verification.notes: I downgraded because the record said '32x-96x across microbenchmarks', but the same page shows 1.52x-6.67x for real I/O, comprehensive and concurrent-task rows. The tier stays C. Metadata is correct: MIT, 5 stars, last commit 2025-07-22, stale, not a fork.
verification.reject_reason: Invalid comparison (enrichment 2026-09-26): no Tokio run in the repo produced the Tokio column. 1.5M is a hard-coded 'literature baseline' constant, 192K is Zokio's own standard-allocator result relabelled, the ~100M/50M/25M/2M/15K rows have no Tokio benchmark code, and the recorded real Tokio runs match none of the figures; the repo's own tokio-comparison.md puts Zokio at 0.84x Tokio on scheduling and 0.59x on I/O. `zig build tokio-vs-zokio` silently prints hard-coded constants as Tokio results when cargo is missing.

name: FasterAPI HTTP/1.1 parser
workload: Unspecified micro-benchmark of the HTTP/1.1 request-line/header parse path, reported as a single per-call nanosecond figure
claimed_speedup: 12ns per parse, described as '40x faster than llhttp API'
tradeoffs: Author states the parser's state machine was itself imported/adapted from llhttp's generated tables rather than being an independent design; project is explicitly framed as an experimental testbed, not a production library.
caveats: No workload, hardware, compiler, or flags are stated anywhere in the doc; the '40x' figure compares calling the imported llhttp state machine directly versus going through llhttp's full public API, which is not a like-for-like comparison of two independent parsers (it likely mostly measures API/wrapper overhead, not parsing-algorithm speed). Treat as a weak, unverified first-party claim. Repo docs folder is literally named 'archive' and the file 'ULTIMATE_ACHIEVEMENT.md', consistent with unreviewed self-marketing copy.
found_via: Blogs / talks: gh search code "than llhttp" -> Ugbot/FasterAPI docs/archive/ULTIMATE_ACHIEVEMENT.md

verification.tier_reason: The page does say '12ns (40x faster than llhttp API)', but llhttp was never measured. The only parser benchmark, benchmarks/fasterapi/bench_http1_parser.cpp, times FasterAPI's own parser and never calls llhttp. docs/archive/ALGORITHM_IMPORT_COMPLETE.md shows the 40x is 12ns divided by a guessed '~500ns' llhttp cost breakdown ('init: ~50ns', 'parse: ~300ns', 'callbacks + copies ~150ns'), so there is no measured comparison with any baseline.
verification.notes: Rejected: the only 'comparison' with llhttp is an estimate, never a benchmark run. The harness note is wrong on one point: the parser does not import llhttp's generated tables, it is hand-written code 'based on' llhttp. Metadata checked and correct (MIT, 2 stars, last commit 2026-05-27, not a fork, not archived).
